name: Thomas B. Marsh
role: First president of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
dateNote: He was baptized on 3 September 1830, ordained an apostle in April 1835, and left the Church in October 1838.
importance: Section 31 was given for him in September 1830, soon after his baptism. Sections 52, 56, and 75 send him on missions, first with Ezra Thayre. As president of the Twelve he received section 112 in 1837, which names him to hold the keys for the Twelve abroad. Section 118 tells him to stay in Missouri to publish, but he left the Church that October.
connections: He was paired with Ezra Thayre and later Selah J. Griffin for missions. Orson Hyde signed a Richmond affidavit with him in October 1838.

sources.title: Thomas Baldwin Marsh, Joseph Smith Papers

reviewNote: Birth, baptism, apostle ordination, presidency of the Twelve, withdrawal (22 October 1838), excommunication (17 March 1839), rebaptism (1857), and death (January 1866, Ogden) checked on JSP. Bare “Thomas” in 31, 112, 118 is not linked.
